title: Definiteness, preliminary agreements, and precontractual liability: editorial notes and questions
summary: Read the surrounding notes and questions alongside the principal cases. The complete assigned pages are preserved here.
notes:
Dixon v. Wells Fargo, N.A.: Dixon separates an enforceable limited assurance during negotiations from agreement on the final transaction. Read it with Drennan and Cyberchron when identifying exactly what reliance protects.

Cyberchron Corp. v. Calldata Systems Development, Inc.: The case separates three bases of recovery: an agreed contract, restitution for a benefit received, and protection of expenses induced by a promise. Only the third supported this appeal.

Channel Home Centers, Division of Grace Retail Corp. v. Grossman: This is a bargained preliminary contract. Compare Dixon and Cyberchron, which use reliance to protect narrower promises without a completed bargain.

Sun Printing & Publishing Ass’n v. Remington Paper & Power Co.: Compare the same judge’s willingness to imply reasonable efforts in Wood and the later willingness to replace failed pricing mechanisms in Oglebay. Identify precisely which open terms matter before treating a contract as indefinite.

Oglebay Norton Co. v. Armco, Inc.: Oglebay connects assent over time, definiteness, reliance-producing investment, gap filling, and specific relief. Its result depends heavily on the established relationship and evidence of continuing commitment.
